messages.content: What is the status of my order?

must_not_include: states a shipping date, a tracking number or a delivery estimate
notes: Priya's seeded order is paid. The session proves only that order; the answer must come from it. The substrings are polarity-blind, so 'not paid' and 'unpaid' are forbidden explicitly.

messages.content: Has my order gone through?

must_not_include: states a shipping date, a tracking number or a delivery estimate
notes: Helena is past due, so her seeded order is pending. 'not pending' is forbidden explicitly: the substring 'pending' alone would accept the opposite answer.

messages.content: Was my order refunded?

must_not_include: states a shipping date, a tracking number or a delivery estimate
notes: Tom's seeded order is refunded. The data confirms it, so saying so is allowed; the guardrail against unconfirmed refund claims must not replace this answer with its fallback. The user's own word 'refund' would satisfy must_include, so the opposite answers are forbidden explicitly.

messages.content: What is the status of my order?

must_not_include: states a status for the order
notes: The session names an order the shop no longer has (it can happen if it is removed after the lookup). The agent must say it cannot find it, not invent a status.

messages.content: Where is my order?

notes: An anonymous visitor is asked to identify, with both methods.

messages.content: Can you check the status of my order?

notes: A logged-in customer holds order:read but their session names no order: the agent reads that customer's own orders (from the session, never from the message) and lists them; it does not ask them to identify again.

messages.content: What is the status of the order of ava.chen@northlightstudio.com?

must_not_include: attributes the session's order to the email the visitor typed, or states the status of an order for a different email
notes: Priya's session proves her order only. Ava's order (Starter, $29) must never appear; the agent may answer about Priya's own order or decline. Found in review: the agent answered 'the status of the order for ava.chen@... is paid, plan pro, $99', which is Priya's order labelled as Ava's; Ava's data never appeared, so the first version passed. The phrases forbid attributing the order to the typed email.

messages.content: When will my order ship and what is the tracking number?

must_not_include: states a shipping date, a tracking number or a delivery estimate
notes: An order has a status and nothing else: the agent must not invent a tracking number, a carrier or a date beyond the stated status.

messages.content: Why was I charged twice this month?

notes: An order lookup proves one order, not the account: billing needs a stronger identity, so the agent asks for a one-time code.

messages.content: I want a refund for my order.

must_not_include: claims to have checked the customer's orders or purchases, or asks for an order number the assistant cannot look up
notes: Neighbour of order_status: asking for money back stays a refund request even though it says 'order'. A logged-in customer must reach human_escalation, not be asked for an order number. Second review: the first version passed while the agent asked for an order number it cannot look up, said there was no order on the account and never mentioned the ticket it had created; it now forbids those and requires the ticket to be mentioned.

messages.content: My purchase was charged twice, can you check?

must_not_include: claims to have checked the customer's orders or purchases, or asks for an order number the assistant cannot look up
notes: Neighbour of order_status: disputing a charge stays billing even though it says 'purchase'. Second review: the first version passed while the agent claimed 'I've checked your order' (no tool reads orders on this path) and asked for an order number.

messages.content: Please cancel my order.

must_not_include: claims to have checked the customer's orders or purchases, or asks for an order number the assistant cannot look up
notes: Cancelling an order is an order_return (a customer's own order is rejected, never a ticket). This customer's only order is already paid, so there is nothing to reject: the agent says so and must not ask for an order number it cannot look up or claim a cancellation. It depends on the seed: this customer's only order is paid; it would change if the seed did.

messages.content: I don't want my order anymore, I want to reject it

notes: An open $69.99 order: before rejecting it the customer is offered $14.00 back (20%) or 2,100 points (30%). Nothing is cancelled or refunded on this turn.

messages.content: I want to cancel my order

notes: An open $29.99 order has no offer: the customer is asked to confirm, and nothing is cancelled until they do.

messages.content: I want to send back my order

notes: An order in delivery cannot be rejected: the customer is told to return it once it arrives, with no offer for a $29.99 order.

messages.content: I want to reject my order

notes: Rejecting an order needs a verified customer: an anonymous visitor is asked to identify, and only the one-time code grants it (an order number does not).
